title: B1 confirmation recognition / readiness gate parity

root_cause.one_line: blocking() defaulted to NO_CONFIRMATIONS, so with no argument it answered a question nobody was asking: what would still block if the operator had signed nothing?
root_cause.classification: another hidden predicate - more precisely, the reader never read the file; a default argument stood in for a decision nobody loaded
not: B1 decision intentionally separate from go-live confirmation
paper readiness ignoring a new schema
root_cause.family: an empty/default value standing in for a real answer - fourth occurrence in this project
root_cause.why_it_still_mattered: a gate that cannot be seen to open is a gate nobody can finish

part_b_trace.consequence: the status command, the readiness report, the dashboard, the ledger and the order executor were all blind to anything the operator ever signed

part_c_fix.unreadable_file_grants: nothing - every gated blocker stays shut

one_was_green_on_the_first_run.which: an unreadable confirmation file grants its flags anyway
one_was_green_on_the_first_run.why_not_a_sleeping_guard: it rewrote the body of an `except` that never fires - load_confirmations answers bad JSON by returning nothing-granted rather than by raising, so the mutation was rewriting UNREACHABLE code and could not have changed any outcome
one_was_green_on_the_first_run.why_that_is_worse: an unreachable guard looks like a safety net in the source, and a real failure later finds nothing underneath it
one_was_green_on_the_first_run.fix: not retargeting the mutation - making the guard reachable on purpose: a test now forces the loader itself to raise and asserts the gate still grants nothing
one_was_green_on_the_first_run.result: the original mutation turns red, because there is finally a path that runs it

part_e_tests.item_11_shown_not_claimed: the preview parses through track1_gates.load_confirmations and is asserted never to parse the confirmation itself
